answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making entry depend on scarce, verifiable endorsements rather than free sign-ups. Each established agent may vouch for only a few newcomers per period, and its own standing is at risk if its endorsees misbehave. A harbor of trusted participants cannot be flooded overnight: an attacker must first earn trust or buy many independent endorsements, and each fake identity leaves an echo in the vouching graph that investigators can trace. Like timber, trust must be grown slowly, so mass-produced identities stay low-privilege until they prove real work.
